Short-form only (30/60/90s presets, 9:16); no long-form/16:9 pipeline, no thumbnail generator, no stated resolution/4K.

jelly_unique_advantages: True pay-per-render at ~$1–7 per long-form video with an itemized receipt, versus $39–$849/mo subscriptions with expiring credits everywhere else.
No stock footage, no avatars: every frame is generated in a locked art style with consistent characters, which is exactly what rivals' users complain they cannot get.
IndexTTS-2 cloned voices with a Voice Tuner and consent-gated uploads, cheaper than ElevenLabs-metered narration on every competitor.
Kimi planner + Gemini scene QA + a 137-rule production doctrine means output is reviewed, not sprayed, which is the monetization-safe posture post July 2025.
Own GPU pipeline (DGX + Modal) so cost per minute is controlled and can be shown honestly before render.
Long-form 16:9 first with a 7-step editor and YouTube OAuth publish; most rivals are 30–90 s vertical tools bolted onto long-form claims.
Invite-only beta with view-as, feedback and changelog already wired, so the 5 target users can be hand-held into paying.
synthesis.one_paragraph_verdict: Jelly already has the hard parts (generated visuals, cloned voices, locked style, YouTube publish, receipts) and most rivals win on legibility and convenience rather than capability, so the month should go to cheap UI over existing engines: show the price before the click, make stills-draft the default with motion as an opt-in second spend, refund failures automatically, add chapters, per-scene motion toggles, overlay toggles, Remix, a pricing calculator, BYO narration and scheduled publish. Skip avatars, stock footage, autopilot series, model menus and subscriptions on purpose and say so on the landing page, because those are the sources of every competitor's 2-star reviews and Jelly's absence of them is the pitch. Multi-language, 9:16 cuts, thumbnail A/B, longer exports and an API are real gaps but belong after the first five payers prove the core loop.
